metaData.originalTitle: Profiling in PyTorch (Part 2): From nn.Linear to a Fused MLP
metaData.title: Profiling in PyTorch (Part 2): From nn.Linear to a Fused MLP
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article profiles a PyTorch MLP, showing how `nn.Linear` fuses bias into the GEMM kernel, how `torch.compile` removes CPU overhead but not GPU kernels for single linears, and how it fuses pointwise ops into a single Triton kernel for the full MLP.
metaData.summary: This is the second part of a series on PyTorch profiling. It builds on Part 1 by replacing a manual matmul-add with `nn.Linear`, then stacking three linears with a GeGLU activation to form an MLP. The article uses detailed profiler traces to explain several key concepts: how `nn.Linear` uses an epilogue to fold bias addition into the GEMM kernel (via `aten::addmm`), why `aten::t` (transpose) is a metadata-only operation with no GPU kernel, and how `torch.compile` removes CPU dispatch overhead (e.g., the transpose view chain) but cannot fuse a single GEMM. For the full MLP, it shows that eager mode launches 5 kernels (3 GEMMs, 1 GeLU, 1 mul), while `torch.compile` fuses the two pointwise ops into a single Triton kernel, reducing the count to 4. The article also explains why different GEMM tile sizes are selected by cuBLAS based on matrix shapes, and how to read kernel names to understand what the GPU is doing.

mainPoints.point: `nn.Linear` fuses bias addition into the GEMM kernel via an epilogue, avoiding a separate kernel launch.
mainPoints.explanation: The `aten::addmm` operation dispatches to a cuBLAS GEMM variant that includes bias addition in its writeback. This is why no separate `aten::add` kernel appears in the profiler trace.

mainPoints.point: `torch.compile` removes CPU dispatch overhead for a single `nn.Linear` but cannot fuse the GEMM kernel itself.
mainPoints.explanation: For a single linear layer, compile folds metadata ops like `aten::t` into the `aten::addmm` call, saving microseconds of CPU work. The GPU kernel remains identical to the eager mode kernel.

mainPoints.point: For an MLP, `torch.compile` fuses pointwise operations (GeLU and multiplication) into a single Triton kernel, reducing kernel launches from 5 to 4.
mainPoints.explanation: In eager mode, the GeGLU MLP launches 3 GEMM kernels, 1 GeLU kernel, and 1 multiplication kernel. Compile fuses the two pointwise ops into one, while the GEMMs remain unchanged.

mainPoints.point: cuBLAS selects different GEMM tile sizes based on matrix dimensions, even when FLOP counts are identical.
mainPoints.explanation: The `down_proj` linear (N=768) uses a 128x256 tile, while `gate_proj` and `up_proj` (N=3072) use a 128x128 tile. This results in a ~10% performance difference despite the same total FLOPs.

keyQuotes: This is worth internalizing. A common reflex is to reach for `torch.compile` whenever a model feels slow. For a single GEMM-with-bias, compile has very little to do.
Forming this expectation before looking is the single most useful habit in the profiling journey: you read the trace to *confirm or break* a guess, not to form one from scratch.
Learning to read this name is one of the most useful habits when comparing traces.

relatedArticles.title: Falcon Perception

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Andrej Karpathy explores the paradigm shift from manual programming to agent orchestration, the automation of AI research, and the profound implications for software engineering and education.

relatedArticles.title: Building a Fast Multilingual OCR Model with Synthetic Data
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details NVIDIA's development of Nemotron OCR v2, a fast and accurate multilingual OCR model trained on a massive, open-source synthetic dataset of 12.2 million images, overcoming data scarcity through a scalable, language-agnostic rendering pipeline.

relatedArticles.title: Beyond the Vector Store: Building the Full Data Layer for AI Applications
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article argues that production AI applications require a hybrid data layer combining vector databases for semantic retrieval with relational databases for transactional integrity, metadata management, and security.

relatedArticles.title: Specialization Beats Scale: A Strategic Variable Most AI Procurement Decisions Overlook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A 3-billion-parameter specialized model outperformed every commercial frontier API in a structured OCR benchmark at roughly fifty times lower cost, demonstrating that distributional alignment to the deployment task can be more decisive than parameter count.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Can Voice Agents Handle Bilingual Customers? Benchmarking Frontier ASR on Code-Switched Speech
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article benchmarks frontier ASR systems on code-switched speech across four language pairs, finding that top models like ElevenLabs Scribe V2, Gemini 3 Flash, and AssemblyAI handle bilingual input with surprisingly small penalties, while errors concentrate on embedded English segments.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni: Long-Context Multimodal Intelligence for Documents， Audio and Video Agents
